skill.name: agent-communication-debugger
skill.description: Diagnoses A2A agent communication failures by checking agent processes, configurations, logs, transport health, routing decisions, and test message delivery.
skill.summary: Debug A2A agent status, routing, transport, and log issues.
skill.author: EGAdams

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are markdown syntax or local diagnostic commands, not Ruby backtick execution or network scanning. Confirmed risks are unredacted secret-check examples and commands that start persistent agent processes; semantic review also found process termination and diagnostic snapshot guidance that can affect local systems or expose data. No prompt injection text was found.

remediation.suggestion: Replace unmasked environment examples with checks that print only whether a variable is set. Avoid echoing real keys in shell history.
Require explicit user confirmation before nohup or pkill commands. Document cleanup steps and prefer foreground diagnostics where possible.
Redact logs, agent configs, and environment metadata before saving or sharing diagnostic bundles.

content.value_statement: Agent systems can fail silently when processes, routing, transports, or keys are misconfigured. This skill guides structured checks across logs, configs, WebSocket status, and test messages.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether orchestrator, coder, tester, and WebSocket processes are running.
Guides inspection of agent.json files for names, topics, capabilities, and JSON syntax.
Searches agent logs for errors, routing decisions, and recent activity.
Verifies WebSocket or message board transport state with local commands.
Runs the included test_message.py script to send and observe a test message.
Maps common symptoms to likely causes and restart steps.
limitations: Designed for the specific A2A project layout shown in the skill files.
Requires local shell access and permission to read logs, configs, and environment metadata.
Does not automatically repair application code or validate every agent implementation.
Diagnostic commands can affect running agents when restart steps are used.

use_cases.title: Restore silent agent workflows
use_cases.description: Find why orchestrator or specialist agents stop receiving or responding to messages.

use_cases.title: Fix wrong routing decisions
use_cases.description: Trace logs and routing rules when requests go to an unexpected agent.

use_cases.title: Run a local health check
use_cases.description: Verify process status, transport connectivity, recent logs, and test message delivery before a demo or deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Check basic agent status
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the agent communication debugger to check whether my orchestrator, coder, tester, and WebSocket agents are running.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose missing responses
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to diagnose why the orchestrator receives messages but no response appears. Check logs, transport, and target agent status.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate wrong routing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the debugging workflow to find why code requests route to the wrong agent. Review discovery, routing logs, priority mappings, and API key state without exposing secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Run complete communication audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a complete A2A communication diagnostic. Summarize process state, configuration validity, transport status, recent errors, message delivery, and safe next actions.

output_examples.input: The coder agent is not responding after the orchestrator accepts a message.
output_examples.output: Report: the orchestrator is running, but the coder agent is stopped. Recent logs show no coder activity. Recommended action: start the coder agent and rerun the message test.

output_examples.input: Requests for code are routing to the dashboard agent.
output: The orchestrator discovered the coder agent.
Routing logs show fallback routing after the LLM decision failed.
The next step is to verify the API key presence without printing the key value.

output_examples.input: Run a complete health check before I test a new agent.
output_examples.output: Summary: process checks, transport status, recent log review, and test message delivery are complete. The report highlights stopped agents, missing config, and safe next actions.

best_practices: Start with read-only checks before using restart or process termination steps.
Mask or omit secret values when reviewing environment variables or .env files.
Capture the exact symptom, expected agent, and recent timestamp before searching logs.
anti_patterns: Do not paste raw API keys, .env contents, or full logs into shared reports.
Do not restart agents until status, logs, and active work are understood.
Do not assume every routing issue is an LLM failure; verify discovery and topics first.

faq.question: What agent systems does this skill support?
faq.answer: It targets the A2A project layout with orchestrator, coder, tester, agent_messaging, storage, and logs directories.

faq.question: Can it send a test message?
faq.answer: Yes. The included test script sends a message to the orchestrator topic and checks for responses.

faq.question: Does it need shell access?
faq.answer: Yes. Many checks use local shell commands to inspect processes, logs, configs, and transport state.

faq.question: Will it expose API keys?
faq.answer: The skill includes some redaction guidance, but users should avoid printing raw environment values or .env contents.

faq.question: Can it restart agents?
faq.answer: It documents restart steps. Users should confirm before stopping or starting processes on shared systems.

faq.question: Does it fix routing logic automatically?
faq.answer: No. It helps identify likely routing causes and points to configuration or code areas to review.
